subject: UC bought Springer's machine summaries
insight: When AI removes the checking in the middle, the cost of checking doesn't vanish — it lands on whoever is last in line
article: The Springer Nature ebooks that UC libraries paid for turned out to include books a machine had summarized, and of the 15 sites built with AI that AudioEye audited, not one reached WCAG A. Taiwan's election deepfake law drew not a single takedown request, and readers handed a faulty AI summary scored 44.8% on memory accuracy — the side that saved the work and the side that absorbed the error were never the same side. So this week, stop counting the hours AI saved you and write down the name of the person doing that checking right now — if there is no name to write, your customer is doing it, and customers don't send an invoice, they just leave.
